bull.b: The sharply expanded backlog provides meaningful forward revenue visibility across launch and Space Systems, reducing reliance on individual contract wins. Its balanced composition and expected near-term conversion support sustained growth while giving management a foundation for production planning and investment.

A high launch success rate and improving production cadence strengthen Rocket Lab’s credibility with commercial and government customers. This operating track record can support repeat bookings, pricing power and greater utilization of launch infrastructure as demand expands.

Substantial liquidity and low reported leverage provide financial flexibility to fund Neutron, expand production and complete the planned Iridium transaction. This reduces near-term solvency pressure and gives Rocket Lab capacity to pursue strategic growth while operating cash flow remains under development.

bear.b: Rocket Lab has not yet converted growing revenue and improved gross margins into sustainable profitability or self-funding cash generation. Continued operating and investment losses can consume liquidity, constrain capital allocation and leave shareholder returns dependent on successful future scaling.

The delayed Neutron debut postpones Rocket Lab’s entry into medium-lift launch and extends the period before the program can broaden its addressable market. Additional testing and an unspecified launch date increase execution uncertainty around customer commitments, spending and future growth.

Neutron development, testing and infrastructure expansion require substantial ongoing investment before the program generates production revenue. Management expects cash flow to remain negative near term, increasing funding needs and delaying the point at which Rocket Lab can consistently finance growth internally.
